open_findings.title: My own module audit reported a wrong count, twice, and the corrected figures are below
open_findings.finding: The verification reviewer caught a fault in tools/orphan_audit.py and tools/module_audit.py that I wrote: both read the shipped-module list with a regex over the WHOLE of tools/build.py, so every entry in UNWIRED_MODULES also matched and was counted as shipped. That inflated the shipped count from 9 to 18.
open_findings.measured_before: Reported: shipped 18, retired 9; '8 of 10 test files load a retired module'.
open_findings.measured_after: Corrected: shipped 9, retired 9, orphans 2 (src/ui/render.js, src/ui/views.js). The misdirection figure is not directly comparable, because the corrected run also picks up the reviewer's declared comparisons as loads. The authority on misdirection is now tests/accept/guard_09_module_scope.cjs, which reads the in-file declarations and fails only on an UNDECLARED retired load: it reports 3, with G04 proving the guard can see a retired module so G02 is not vacuous.
open_findings.impact: The earlier figure overstated the problem. The substantive finding still stands - the view-layer test suite loads orphans that do not ship, the two view layers are not equivalent, and the build's guard could not see modules in neither list.
open_findings.handling: Both tools fixed to read only the region before UNWIRED_MODULES. tools/module_audit.py now states in its own output that it is a raw text scan and names the guard as the check, so a future reader does not act on the raw number. I have not re-derived every figure I reported from the faulty tool.

open_findings.title: A unit mismatch would have overstated every tax-inclusive competitor price by about 20%
open_findings.finding: src/data/evidence.js adjustToComparable() computes net = value / (1 + rate / 100), so it expects a VAT rate as a PERCENTAGE. The payload stores it as a FRACTION (vat: 0.2). Nothing reconciled the two and neither the field name nor the row stated the unit. Handing 0.2 to that rule divides by 1.002, removing 0.2% of tax instead of 20%.
open_findings.measured: For AUTODOC UK at 76.99 GBP including 20% VAT, at the payload's own documented 1.17 EUR/GBP: the correct net is EUR 75.07, and taking vat=0.2 as a percentage gives EUR 89.90, an overstatement of 19.8%. Verified with tools/_vat_unit_probe.cjs.
open_findings.unit_resolved_by_the_data: The payload proves its own unit rather than requiring an assumption: its net column equals price / (1 + vat) on 5 of 5 rows that state price, vat and net, including all 3 rows where the two units would give different answers. The two rows that also fit a percentage are the zero-VAT rows, where both units trivially agree. So the field is a fraction, and the net column is the proof.
open_findings.impact: An advertised competitor price would have appeared roughly a fifth higher than it is, which is the direction that argues our own net terms are too high. That is precisely the misuse MARKET-05 exists to prevent, so the two faults would have reinforced each other.
open_findings.handling: src/data/comparable.js now refuses to infer the unit from the size of the number - it requires the row to declare percent or fraction, and otherwise returns VAT_RATE_UNIT_NOT_STATED and leaves the row unresolved. The market agent found this by first producing the wrong number and being caught by its own test. The defect remains live in src/data/evidence.js, which is the shared rule; declaring vat_rate_unit on the observation records, or holding the rate as a fraction end to end, is the durable fix and is not yet applied.
open_findings.owner: integration owner (shared rule and the observation records)

open_findings.title: The payload currently contains no comparison that can be made, and the new panel is not assembled or wired
open_findings.finding: Two separate gaps. First, src/data/comparable.js is not in tools/build.py MODULES and nothing calls it, so it ships nothing and has no screen - a deliberate constraint, because the view layer was owned by another agent while it was written. Second, the exclusions on the real payload are dominated by PRODUCT_MATCH_UNRESOLVED and PACK_CONTENTS_UNKNOWN: every payload offer is matched on a seller cross-reference rather than exact equivalence, and no offer declares whether its quote is for a piece or a pack. So the eligible set is empty on the authorised data.
open_findings.measured: python tools/orphan_audit.py lists src/data/comparable.js as an orphan. node --test tests/market_evidence.test.mjs -> 32 pass / 0 fail, so the logic is exercised on fixtures rather than on the payload.
open_findings.impact: MARKET-07 exists as tested logic with no visible output, and the commercial question it answers cannot be answered from the current data. This is the honest position rather than a working panel.
open_findings.handling: Wiring needs two edits not yet made: add comparable.js to MODULES, and have app.js call it. The data gap needs the source to state pack contents and exact equivalence, which no code change supplies.
open_findings.owner: integration owner (wiring) + source owner (equivalence and pack contents)

open_findings.title: The shipped export builder still has no identity or attachment permission code
open_findings.finding: The allowlist and the free-text refusal are now in the shipped src/data/export.js, and the acceptance suite is green on the export. But the retired src/output/recipients.js exports 22 names including makeDevIdentity, requireApprovedIdentity, canRead, canAttach and findRestrictedInBytes, and the shipped module has no equivalent. Repointing the byte-level test at the shipped builder failed 9 of 11 for exactly this reason.
open_findings.impact: F08's data-disclosure half is closed. Its access-control half is not: permission for a participant to read a record, and refusal of a restricted attachment, are not implemented in what ships.
open_findings.handling: Wire the permission surface into the shipped builder, or state the restriction plainly as unimplemented. A browser-side allowlist is not access control, and no backend exists here to provide it.

open_findings.title: Two view layers exist, they are not equivalent, and the tests load the one that does not ship
open_findings.finding: tools/build.py ships src/ui/app.js. src/ui/views.js and src/ui/render.js are in NEITHER the shipped list NOR the retired list, so the build's guard cannot see them. Both are loaded by tests/ux_flow.test.mjs, so that suite's result describes a layer the product does not run. The two are the same size (app.js 99172 bytes, views.js 77713) and not equivalent: the F05 guard is in app.js and absent from views.js; the UX-06 amber unavailable state is absent from app.js and present in views.js.
open_findings.handling: Reconcile into the shipped layer, then retire the orphans deliberately. In progress.

open_findings.title: The candidate records carry no reporting period, and the source cannot supply one
open_findings.finding: ACCEPT-01 R27 fails, and it should stay failing. The 10,543 candidate rows have no period, year or date field. The screening rule is described as running on 2025/2024 and H1 2026/2025, and none of those values is on the rows. Two rows also carry a null cost reconciliation because the price-file FOB value is empty for 5876150530 and 5876150531 - a null difference is not a match.
open_findings.impact: Nothing on the candidate screen can be promoted on its own evidence until a caller supplies a period it states itself. Guessing the period would be an invention.
open_findings.handling: Needs a commercial or source input, not a code change. Recorded as undeclared and left visible.

open_findings.title: The payload still declares a split cost basis across alternatives
open_findings.finding: The ranking resolves every row to one offer date and reports a single baseline, so the screen no longer shows two baselines. The underlying payload still declares the split: the no-action rows for pads, cabin filter and oil filter use SEP26 while some alternatives use OCT26.
open_findings.handling: Data work, not a code fix.

open_findings.title: The oil migration cannot be calculated from the payload as supplied
open_findings.finding: Both product lines' parts costs are present and the Genuine line's list price appears in the option's prose, but no transferred quantity is stated anywhere and there is no applicable net selling price for the Genuine part number 8982705240. The result is correctly unresolved rather than a fabricated zero.
open_findings.handling: Needs a stated transferred quantity and an applicable net selling price for the Genuine number.

open_findings.title: A country name appears where a distributor name is expected in the candidate rows
open_findings.finding: Candidate rows carry distributor labels ITUK and PORTUGAL. PORTUGAL is a country, and the worked cases use ITUK and the I Motors / Portugal account. The source never states which legal entity PORTUGAL is.
open_findings.handling: Not renamed - renaming would invent the entity. Kept visible with every label as it appears. ITUK and IUK are separate entities and UTI and UMI must never be blended.

open_findings.title: A reported byte figure was not measured and is not in the record
open_findings.finding: The export agent reported that the pre-fix brief leaked 1013 bytes. Its own test file contains no such value, so the figure was not produced by a command. Its actual work checks out on the numbers that can be measured.
open_findings.handling: Excluded from the record. The measured position is used instead: 426 bytes before the container fix, 944 after, and 11/0 on the byte-level check against the shipped builder.
